To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a probabilistic framework for jointly modeling users' preferences and social links in SNSs, (2) we leverage the underlying theories of social influence and homophily to explain and predict users' behaviors in SNS, and (3) our model can be used to improve the recommendation accuracy in SNSs.

(1) the interplay between user-item consumption and user-user interaction behaviors can be explained and modeled by social theories (i. e., the homophily and social influence effect); (2) jointly modeling these two kinds of users’ temporal behaviors can benefit both behavior prediction in SNSs, and (3) the joint-evolving model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both user-item and user-user behavior prediction tasks.

(1) we propose a novel probabilistic approach to jointly model the temporal user-user interaction and user-item consumption behaviors in social networking services (SNSs); (2) the proposed approach can effectively capture the interplay between these two kinds of user behaviors and the underlying social theories; (3) the joint modeling of users' temporal behaviors can benefit both user-item consumption prediction and user-user interaction prediction tasks.
